header: Here are the shapes of a read health check-up roster (one record per employee: ticket, name, department as printed and the CHECK-UP DATE) and the two helpers every reading uses. I keep the reading itself in geminiSchedule.ts (Gemini).

symbols.name: EXTRACT_VERSION
doc: Bump this number whenever the reading changes what it returns.

symbols.name: ScheduleTimeBudgetError
doc: I throw this from the roster reading when deps.shouldStop() says the time is up. Nothing has been stored; the caller decides what to do (the upload saves the circular anyway).

members.name: dateFromOtherPage
doc: This is true when the date is printed on the other side of a page break, because the cell goes on over it.

members.name: y
doc: Height of the row on the straightened page image; I keep it for looking at the row again.

members.name: ticketAlt
doc: Other readings of the ticket (they lost the vote); the HR directory may confirm one of them.

members.name: codeAlt
doc: Other readings of the department code; they lost the vote.

members.name: codeNote
doc: Set when I changed the department code because it did not belong to the department printed on the row.

members.name: warnings
doc: Things a person should look at: a group of an odd size, dates out of order, rows without a date ...

members.name: info
doc: Pages that are not roster pages (the covering letter). That is normal, not a problem.

members.name: groups
members.type: Array<{ date: string | null; rows: number }>
doc: How many rows each date covers, in order.

symbols.name: HEADING
doc: I do not count the table's own heading cells ("SL.NO", "T.NO", "NAME", "DEPTT. CODE", "DEPARTMENT", "DATE") as people.

symbols.name: isEmployeeRow
symbols.sig: export function isEmployeeRow(ticket: string | null, name: string, code: string | null, department: string): boolean
doc: Is this row an employee? I say yes when it has a readable ticket, or a name together with a department code. A row with only a serial number (the digit strip can put one on the heading row) or whose "name" is a column heading is not an employee.

symbols.name: cleanTicket
symbols.sig: export function cleanTicket(raw: string): string | null
doc: 6 digits, or null. A rule next to the digits is often read as a 7th character ("[333787", "1318839"): I drop it when that is what it is.
